title: Differentials of parameters in a DVR with finite separable residue field
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian local $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] which is a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Write $\mathfrak m$ for its maximal ideal and $\kappa=A/\mathfrak m$ for its residue field, endowed with the induced field extension of $k$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Assume $\kappa/k$ is finite and separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Let $d:A\to\Omega_{A/k}$ be the universal Kähler derivation [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], and suppose that $\Omega_{A/k}$ is free of rank one as an $A$-module. For every $t\in A$ with $\mathfrak m=tA$, the class of $t$ in $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ is nonzero and $dt\otimes1\ne0$ in $\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A\kappa$. Moreover, for every basis $e$ of $\Omega_{A/k}$, the unique coefficient $a\in A$ with $dt=ae$ is a unit. In particular, $A\to\Omega_{A/k}$, $b\mapsto b\,dt$, is an $A$-linear isomorphism with inverse $ce\mapsto ca^{-1}$.

proof.text: The finite extension $\kappa/k$ is finitely generated as a field: any finite $k$-vector-space basis generates it as a field, because it already spans it linearly. It is also separable in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. Indeed, for any finitely generated intermediate field $F$, every $x\in F$ is algebraic, and its minimal polynomial over $k$ is the same whether $x$ is regarded in $F$ or in $\kappa$ (the evaluation kernels in $k[T]$ agree). Hence every such polynomial is separable by [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. The empty family is a transcendence basis of the algebraic extension $F/k$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis] (it is algebraically independent, $k(\emptyset)=k$, and $F/k$ is algebraic), and $F/k$ is separable algebraic, so $F/k$ is separably generated. This verifies exactly the separability convention of the next cited lemma.

source.place: Tag 030O (definition-separable-field-extension); algebraic case and finite field generation, unpacked from the definitions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-separable-residue-cotangent-injective] with $R=A$. Noetherianity, locality and the $k$-algebra structure are hypotheses of this item; the preceding step verifies finite field generation and the precise separability notion. Its map sends $t\bmod\mathfrak m^2$ to $dt\otimes1$. By its injectivity and Step 1 this image is nonzero in $\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A\kappa$.

Let $e$ be any rank-one basis of $\Omega_{A/k}$. By the unique-coordinate description of a basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module], write $dt=ae$ with unique $a\in A$. If $a\in\mathfrak m$, tensor balancing gives $dt\otimes1=e\otimes\bar a=0$, contrary to Step 3. Thus $a\notin\mathfrak m$ and $a$ is a unit: in a local ring the nonunits form its maximal ideal. This argument applies to every choice of $e$.

source.place: Tag 0C1E (lemma-uniformizer-works), final sentence: the rank-one unit-coefficient calculation, written out.

proof.text: For this basis and coefficient define $\psi(ce)=ca^{-1}$. Unique coordinates make $\psi$ well defined and $A$-linear. The map $\phi(b)=b\,dt=ba e$ is $A$-linear, and $\psi(\phi(b))=baa^{-1}=b$, while $\phi(\psi(ce))=ca^{-1}ae=ce$. Hence $\phi$ is an isomorphism with exactly the stated inverse. Since $t$ was arbitrary, every assertion holds for every generator of $\mathfrak m$.
